negative_results.proposition_refuted: A per-run host capability token may be embedded into generated target code without affecting deterministic compiler identity.
negative_results.observation: The v1 generated-code SHA changed across executions because a freshly generated capability-token hash was compiled into the target.
negative_results.impact: Capability instances must be runtime resources/handles or separately receipted deployment data, not compiler-output identity inputs unless contract identity explicitly requires that distinction.

negative_results.proposition_refuted: Passing an inherited file descriptor into an ordinary unrestricted Python process is sufficient proof of a production capability sandbox.
negative_results.observation: The v2 test constrains the generated probe path, but the Python runtime itself is not sandboxed against arbitrary ambient host APIs/imports.
negative_results.impact: Production acceptance requires OS/runtime enforcement and typed opaque host resource semantics in addition to source-level capability references.

negative_results.proposition_refuted: The current mandatory ClayCode interconnect preflight can execute against the current trigger registry without governance drift.
negative_results.observation: Registry peer set contains clayresearch; research_interconnect_preflight.py explicit PRIORITY tables still contain clay and intentionally raise RuntimeError when sets differ.
negative_results.impact: Strong mesh completion/promotion is fail-closed until the rename is synchronized across preflight/validators/protocol tables; this run records but does not silently bypass the blocker.
